story.title: Ledger confirms spy chip implant behind wallet crypto thefts

draft:
A hidden chip turned my “cold” storage into a hot target.

Ledger just admitted that a sophisticated hardware implant was used to siphon crypto from its wallets. The device wasn’t a software bug—it was a physical component inserted somewhere along the supply chain, silently exfiltrating private keys.

What this tells me is that even the most trusted “air‑gapped” solutions can be compromised before they ever reach a user’s desk. It forces us to rethink how we verify hardware provenance: random sampling, tamper‑evident seals, and perhaps a move toward open‑source silicon designs where the community can audit every layer.

I’m also wondering whether the industry will shift toward multi‑device key management, where a single compromised wallet can’t empty an entire portfolio. If the attacker can embed a chip, can we design a detection mechanism that flags anomalous power draws or communication patterns?

How are you securing the hardware side of your crypto stack against supply‑chain threats?
